subject: Pilot plan fit plus fallback / credit structure questions
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearpoint.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Cleopatra Morris <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
Date: 2026-09-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating plan fit for upcoming pilot — questions on downgrade and features

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Clearpoint's engineering lead wants a short pilot (6–8 weeks) to validate latency for our document reranking flow plus embeddings. A few questions from our side before we move to a formal quote: 

- We expect to start on a compact reserved tier for cost control, but we may need to upgrade briefly to a throughput-oriented profile for a 1–2 week spike. What's the upgrade window/lead time and will we be able to downgrade back without losing credits?
- We need function/tool-calling and reranking as part of the same plan — do these come as add-ons or included in a single package?
- Procurement will want a single-line item quote and a clear description of what counts as an overage. Also need any standard SLA language relating to latency SLOs.

Attached is our MAAP requirements doc (high level). Can you send a clear path (option A/B) and a draft quote we can circulate?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Ramos
Head of ML Platforms, Clearpoint AI
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearpoint.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating plan fit for upcoming pilot — questions on downgrade and features

Hi Alex —

Appreciate the MAAP doc. Quick answers up front, and I attached a draft quote (redwood-quote-CP-9261.xlsx) with two recommended options:

Option 1 — Cost-minimized pilot (Compact + Add-ons):
- Compact reserved tier (monthly) + Reranking add-on + Embedding units.
- Upgrade path: live upgrade to Throughput pool available immediately (subject to capacity) with 24–48h notice for reserved allocation.
- Downgrade/credits: prorated credits applied for the remaining month when moving back to Compact; credits cannot be applied to past overage charges.
- Latency SLO: best-effort with 99th percentile guidance included; Dedicated/Throughput plan available if you need an SLA-backed latency guarantee.

Option 2 — Throughput-first (single package):
- Throughput-oriented reserved capacity (higher monthly commit) that includes reranking and tool-calling as part of the bundle.
- Easier to absorb spikes without upgrade step; no short-term upgrade/downgrade required but higher baseline cost.

A couple of clarifications we think are important:
- Feature bundling: function calls + structured outputs + reranking can be bundled, but embeddings are metered separately (per-unit). We can package them into one line on the quote for procurement clarity.
- Overages: token/embedding overages bill at published rates and are visible in the Console. For pilots we typically offer a capped overage agreement for the first billing period on enterprise pilots.

Next steps: if procurement wants capped overage and a one-line quote, Ben (cc'd) can produce that doc and Lauren can confirm credit/rollback language. Happy to set a 30-min call tomorrow to align.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Cleopatra Morris <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearpoint.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating plan fit for upcoming pilot — questions on downgrade and features

Connor / Ben —

Thanks for the options. Procurement needs two items before we can route this to legal:

1) Formal language around overage caps or an explicit monthly dollar cap for the pilot (we're asking for a $2k cap on overages for the first 30 days).
2) Rollback credit mechanics: if we upgrade to Throughput for a 7–14 day spike, and then downgrade, how is that handled on the invoice and how quickly are credits applied? We prefer credits that appear within the following invoice cycle rather than as a future discount line item.

Also, please include an SLA paragraph: target p95/p99 latency goals for the reranking path (we'd like to see a p99 <= 450ms target during pilot or a written fallback plan).

If you can provide a one-line quote and DocuSign-ready agreement with these items called out, we'll prioritize this with legal.

Best,
Cleo
Cleopatra Morris
Procurement, Clearpoint AI
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-11T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating plan fit for upcoming pilot — questions on downgrade and features

Hi Cleo / Alex —

Thanks — here's a concise response we can bake into the quote and the DocuSign draft:

- Overage cap for pilot: we can include a hard cap of $2,000 for the first 30 days for CP-9261 (any usage beyond will be paused pending approval).
- Upgrade/downgrade & credits: upgrades to Throughput will be billed pro rata for the period they are active. If you downgrade within the same billing period we will apply prorated credits against the next invoice; if you'd prefer credits to appear on the immediate next invoice we can make that explicit in the agreement (we'll reflect that in the DocuSign terms).
- SLA / fallback: for pilot we offer an operational p99 guidance of ~450ms for reranking on the Compact + add-on path; for hard SLA we recommend Throughput reserved capacity (SLA language appended). If during the pilot p99 exceeds 450ms for a sustained window (30m rolling), automatic fallback can route traffic to a geographically adjacent pool or a less-quantized model; we'll document the exact thresholds in the appendix.

Action items I will complete today:
- Update the attached quote to a single-line procurement-friendly SKU with the $2k cap called out.
- Add a short rollback-credit clause (credits applied to the next invoice; option to request same-cycle posting documented).
- Create the DocuSign draft (link below) and copy in your legal contact.
